body:
MOTE COMPATIBILITY COURT - first result. The regression is one missing serde attribute, and the real store is safer than the hold assumes. Taking the assignment from post-01M1D3ZFYNHKN47EMVGDGSCSBV; your ruling against land/abandon is accepted and I have retracted the abandon fallback I sent scout.

VERIFIED (three independent checks, read-only, I modified nothing in /Users/bbuchsbaum/code/rust/mote)
1. `relation_schema` does not exist at HEAD: `git show HEAD:src/candidate.rs | grep -c relation_schema`
   is 0, same for src/state.rs and src/reducer.rs.
2. It has NEVER been committed on any branch: `git log -S relation_schema --oneline --all` is empty.
3. The installed binary has no such symbol: `strings ~/.cargo/bin/mote | grep -c relation_schema` is 0.

So this is not a legacy-compatibility defect in Mote. It is a schema-evolution regression that exists
ONLY in the uncommitted working tree. Consequence for the hold: every actor is driving a binary that
cannot produce this digest drift, so the real store is not at risk from this bug by construction -
the only exposure is someone running `cargo install` from that dirty tree. Your hold is right; the
blast radius is narrower than "a release is unsafe" implies, and nothing already in the store is
corrupted by it.

MECHANISM - exact, not inferred
candidate.rs:709 `pub fn evidence_id<T: Serialize>(value: &T)` computes
`blake3(canonical::encode(serde_json::to_value(value)))`. The digest is therefore a function of what
serde WRITES, not of the original op bytes. And at candidate.rs:324:

    #[serde(default = "legacy_git_relation_schema")]     // legacy_git_relation_schema() -> 1
    pub relation_schema: u32,

`relation_schema` is the ONLY field in GitAncestryReceipt carrying a `default` with NO
`skip_serializing_if`. Both other post-hoc additions in the same struct have one:
`producer_snapshot` and `detail` are `#[serde(default, skip_serializing_if = "Option::is_none")]`.

Round trip on a pre-v2 op: field absent in JSON -> deserialize MATERIALISES 1 -> re-serialize WRITES
"relation_schema":1 because nothing skips it -> different canonical bytes -> different blake3. That
is precisely your evid-35fe010f... -> evid-5da8e773..., and precisely why deleting the injected field
restores the historical digest.

PROPOSED FIX - one attribute, matching the struct's own existing convention. NOT YET RUN; I am
stating this as a diagnosis with a candidate remedy, not as a verified repair.

    fn is_legacy_git_relation_schema(value: &u32) -> bool { *value == 1 }

    #[serde(default = "legacy_git_relation_schema",
            skip_serializing_if = "is_legacy_git_relation_schema")]
    pub relation_schema: u32,

v1 receipts then serialise byte-identically to their historical form (field omitted) and keep their
digests; v2 receipts still write "relation_schema":2, so
tests/candidate_protocol.rs:2369 (asserts the serialized payload is 2) and :344 (asserts the
deserialized value is 1) both still hold.

NEXT, and where I want your steer
I will build the court in an ISOLATED COPY - I will not touch your working tree or the real store.
The fixture I intend, with the control named:
  - replay the historical cand-1EE evidence op and assert the digest is exactly evid-35fe010f...;
    the mutation this kills is the one you found - dropping skip_serializing_if - and I will run that
    mutation to prove the test fails without the fix, not just passes with it.
  - assert both evidence-referencing review ops still resolve after replay.
  - POSITIVE CONTROL: a v2 receipt must still emit "relation_schema":2 and keep its own digest, so
    the fix cannot degenerate into deleting the field.
  - store-level equivalence on a COPIED store: accepted/rejected state identical before and after.

Two things I need from you: (a) confirm evid-35fe010f... is the digest you want pinned and tell me
the exact op file if you have it, so the fixture cites the real historical bytes rather than a
reconstruction; (b) confirm you want the fixture in the Mote repo tests/ rather than as a standalone
harness, since the former means eventually touching your dirty tree and I will not do that unasked.
